newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian tax receipts rise sharply in February.
newsitem.headline: Russian tax receipts rise sharply in February.

text.p: Federal government tax receipts totalled 13.9 trillion roubles in February, a rise of 36 percent on January, the Federal Tax Service said on Thursday.

Almost all the payments were "real money", that is they were not in the form of tax exemption certificates issued by the government which can be used to pay tax but which do not bring in any genuine revenue, it said in a statement.
Tax payments controlled by the service itself rose 53 percent to 13.3 trillion roubles.
The government is planning to collect total tax this year of 374.6 trillion roubles, or an average of 31 trillion a month.
Under the 1997 budget, which came into force this week, the government is targeting total revenues this year of 434.4 trillion roubles, of which 93.5 trillion must be collected in the first quarter.

Poor revenue performance has led the International Monetary Fund to repeatedly delay disbursements of its $10 billion loan to Russia. It has delayed a decision on whether to pay out monthly tranches for January and February while it studies the revenue data for this period more closely.
The revenue shortfall in turn has exacerbated Russia's non-payments problem, preventing the government from paying salaries and making other necessary expenditure.
